question.text: Which statement about Category III AIFs is CORRECT in the context of investment strategies?

answer.text: Cat III AIFs can take leverage and derivative positions to generate absolute returns over medium-to-long term.
Cat III AIFs cannot invest in derivatives.
Cat III AIFs must only invest intra-day.
Cat III AIFs are restricted to equity long-only.

explanation.text: The Logic: Section 10.1.1 opening: Cat III AIFs 'may take leverage, short positions and derivative positions, in order to generate absolute returns over medium and long term'. Intra-day is explicitly NOT the intent. The Trap: A is factually wrong. C inverts the chapter. D ignores all non-equity strategies. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-D: Cat I/II cannot leverage. XIX-C covers Cat III permission. Manager's Pro-Tip: The 'medium-to-long-term' framing is crucial when marketing Cat III — do NOT pitch intra-day P&L; SEBI has flagged this in past inspections. All P&L narratives should be on minimum quarterly horizon.
